summary: Add a read-only vacation wallchart at /org/{orgId}/time-off/calendar and the two stated country columns the holidays behind it now follow. Two nullable Char(2) columns land (Membership.countryCode, Organization.countryCode); one shared helper resolveMemberHolidayCountry(membership, organization) replaces the four places that read Account.phoneCountryCode to decide a member's holiday country, so the chain has one implementation and the phone is dropped as a source everywhere at once. One new capability ships in both unions (ViewTimeOffCalendar in roles.ts, view-time-off-calendar in index.ts), gating one new read endpoint that answers 404 rather than 403. Two new endpoints carry the organization country (GET and PUT .../settings/country, both 404-gated on ViewHolidays / ManageHolidays); the member country rides the shipped member read and write, which keep every status and message they have and refuse an invalid code with the 400 they already refuse an invalid role with. Three screens: the new calendar page and nav row, one Select on Settings > Holidays, one Select in the member About block. Nothing is written by the calendar and no vacation math is recomputed.

tasks.title: The two nullable country columns and one additive migration

migration.note: One migration adding two nullable columns with no default: Membership.countryCode String? @db.Char(2) and Organization.countryCode String? @db.Char(2). No table, no rename, no drop, no new NOT NULL, no backfill. infra/deploy.sh runs prisma migrate deploy, from the image it is about to deploy, as step 5 of 6 — BEFORE the Terraform rollout of the services (infra/deploy.sh:27: '**Migrations run BEFORE the rollout**, and the order is the whole point'), because new code against an old schema 500s on every query touching a column the migration has not added. Additive is what makes the reverse safe — old code against the new schema simply does not select these columns — so a code rollback needs no database rollback. Membership.countryCode is the one a reviewer misses: the feature reads as organization-scoped and it is not.
migration.reverseSafe: Both columns land null on every existing row, so the migration alone changes no observed behaviour. The chain is evaluated on read (REQ-01-026), so no stored value can be wrong in the meantime.

concurrency.lock: none — DDL only; both columns are added nullable so no row is rewritten and no existing writer's transaction changes shape

tasks.notes: Holiday.countryCode is already String? @db.Char(2) (schema.prisma:916) — the two new columns take that exact type so all three compare the same way.

tasks.notes: Two different predicates are both called 'a valid alpha-2 value' in this spec and they are deliberately not the same one. The WRITE (Validation Rule 9, REQ-01-036, REQ-01-051) is the shipped shape check: validateHolidayCountryCode (packages/validation/src/holidays.ts:93) against COUNTRY_CODE_PATTERN = /^[A-Z]{2}$/ (holidays.ts:34) — it refuses 'pl' rather than upcasing it and it ACCEPTS 'XX', which is what makes REQ-01-027 and Edge case 10 reachable at all. The READ (REQ-01-026, REQ-01-027, REQ-01-040) must upcase and then test membership of the 249-code ISO list, because TC-01-UNIT-01 requires 'pl' -> 'PL' and 'XX'/'YY' -> not usable. Do NOT build resolveMemberHolidayCountry on validateHolidayCountryCode: it would return 'XX' as usable and refuse 'pl', failing TC-01-UNIT-01 on both branches, and it is exactly the mistake HolidaysService.normalizeResolvedCountry makes today (holidays.service.ts:381). tasks.title: GET /api/organizations/{orgId}/time-off/calendar — the read the screen is built on

migration.note: no schema change in this task

allCallSites: apps/api/src/time-off/time-off-calendar.controller.ts#read (new; the address answers 404 today — no controller in apps/api/src maps time-off/calendar, verified)

concurrency.lock: none — the calendar writes nothing. Invariant 1 of the State Machine: it never writes a VacationRequest, a VacationReserveTransaction or a Holiday, and TC-01-INT-12 and TC-01-INT-14 both assert no membership was written by a read.

tasks.notes: Gate: SessionGuard + OrgScopeGuard on the class, then `can(normalizeRole(role), 'view-time-off-calendar')` in the service throwing a bare NotFoundException — never @RequireCapability, whose guard answers 403, and the refusal must be byte-identical to the wrong-organization 404 (REQ-01-002 and REQ-01-039). Hand the check the NORMALIZED role: a membership still storing 'member' normalizes to 'user' (roles.ts:32, LEGACY_ALIASES) and must be answered 200, because the sidebar draws its row from hasCapability, which normalizes — handing can() the raw stored value is the dead navigation REQ-01-004 forbids and is what TC-01-UNIT-04's last probe fails on. Validation order is Validation Rule 1..9 with the FIRST failure the whole answer: range required, range inverted, range too wide, scope invalid, teams/people required, then the row cap over the RESOLVED rows. Dates: VacationRequest.startDate/endDate and Holiday.date are all @db.Date (schema.prisma:742, 744, 912) — compare against the raw ISO range and never against a tz-shifted instant, which is what TC-01-INT-10 fails a DATE-against-TIMESTAMPTZ comparison on. `range.today` alone comes from Account.timezone, falling back to UTC on null, '' or an unrecognized zone (Edge case 18; the stored column is null until a member sets one and the account read projects that as '' — account.service.ts hands back the stored value and the settings read coerces). Scope resolution: all = every active membership; teams = the union of ProjectMember rows on the named projects (one row per membership, never one per assignment — ProjectMember is @@unique([projectId, membershipId]), schema.prisma:1016, and the union still needs a distinct over memberships); the `none` sentinel additionally returns every active membership with no ProjectMember row on any NON-archived project (Project.status, schema.prisma:784) — that archived flag is read ONLY by the none bucket, never by the named-project branch (Edge case 5). projectIds and memberIds are intersected with session.organizationId BEFORE they reach a where clause, so a foreign id is dropped rather than answered (REQ-01-010). holidays[] carries every holiday dated inside the window whatever country it names; holidayIds per member is the chain's OUTPUT, and appliesToAllInView is computed per holiday against the rows THIS response carries and no others. Bands carry the true startDate and endDate plus the two edge flags — clipped in the paint, never in the payload — and workingDays is the frozen column, never a recount. Emit no financial field and no MemberProfile field: TC-01-INT-01 asserts the absence over the whole body, and MemberProfile.country sits behind ViewMemberProfilePii and is never read here.

doubleBehavioursNote: None. This spec has no External Contracts section and names no system we do not own: no third-party call, no key, no MCP server, no new secret and no new AWS resource. The cases file states it outright under 'Access this needs' — 'None. Every observation above was made against this repository's own API on its own ports.' There is therefore no Assumed row carrying a requirement, and nothing to build a double from.

dsGaps.missing: An absence-band colour set — the approved fill and border, the pending hatch and dashed border, the band label, and the legend's two swatches
dsGaps.resolution: Declared once on the calendar page's own root as --surface-timeoff-band, --border-timeoff-band and --text-timeoff-band and read through var() everywhere a band, its border, its hatch or its label is drawn, so no colour on this screen is a literal. Violet, which none of --status-success, --status-warning, --status-error, --status-info or --color-holiday uses, so a band reads as a category and not as a claim about how somebody is doing. Closed by the three names entering @ds as time-off category tokens with the page's local block deleted in the same change — the policy catalogue wants a colour per absence type and this is the first of that set. Never improvised per element.

dsGaps.missing: A layout token for a pinned first column
dsGaps.resolution: --name-col: 264px, declared beside the three colours and referenced by every row's grid-template-columns. Closed by a pinned-first-column token in @ds, which the reports tables would take as well.

Two 3px measures stay as literals, each carrying an @literal comment and its reason: the margin on each side of a band, which is what separates two adjacent bands and which 4px would eat the day column for; and the 3px stripe of the pending hatch in the legend swatch — note this is the LEGEND swatch's stripe (mock :97, 0 3px / transparent 3px 6px), not the band's own hatch (mock :164-165, 0 4px / transparent 4px 8px), which is not below --space-1. Closed by a sub---space-1 step in @ds or a band-gap token.

dsSettled: Three measures that would otherwise have been improvised are already answered by the package and must not be re-declared: the band's height is --space-10, the legend swatch's corner is --radius-s, and the two segmented controls are ToggleButton with the track, pill and shadow that component owns. Drawing a segmented control on this page would put a second shadow colour beside the package's and a second keyboard beside its roving tab stop.

risks.risk: The member About save button is disabled unless the form is dirty, and dirty is computed from role and jobTitle only (MemberDetailScreen.tsx:169-171, :316). Adding the country Select without adding it to dirty produces a control that changes and never saves, and TC-01-E2E-08's 'one save, one toast' cannot be observed.
risks.mitigation: T8 extends the dirty computation to the country. Note this is a pre-existing disabled-for-state button on a shipped screen, not a new one; the repository rule about never disabling for validation is not being widened here, and nothing in this spec asks for that button's behaviour to change beyond including the new field.

risks.risk: The read chain and the write validator mean two different things by 'a valid alpha-2 value', and reusing validateHolidayCountryCode for the read is the natural mistake — it is what HolidaysService.normalizeResolvedCountry does today. That single reuse fails TC-01-UNIT-01 on two branches at once ('pl' refused instead of upcased, 'XX' returned instead of skipped) and silently breaks REQ-01-027 and REQ-01-040.
risks.mitigation: T2 names both predicates and their files explicitly. TC-01-UNIT-01's ('XX','PL') and ('XX','YY') pairs are the discriminating cases and they run in under a second.

risks.risk: Dropping Account.phoneCountryCode as a holiday source moves money on Amounts Owed the moment T3 lands, and it moves it DOWN first: a member whose only country was their phone's resolves to null and stops receiving that country's holiday rows until somebody states a country. The spec's own probe measured the shape — one PL holiday produced one holiday row (320.00) against five (1280.00) for a global day in a five-member fixture.
risks.mitigation: Not a code mitigation: stating the organization country on Settings > Holidays in the same change window as the deploy is the step, and it restores and then widens what was being paid. It belongs in the release note. The migration alone changes nothing because both columns land null and the chain is evaluated on read, so nothing is stored wrong in the meantime and a rollback needs no data repair.

risks.risk: T3 changes four call sites that three shipped E2E suites cover (reports-amounts-owed, reports-time-and-activity, reports-time-off) and one integration suite (holidays). Those suites are the backward-compatibility enforcement named in the README and this area does not otherwise touch them.
risks.mitigation: Run them targeted after T3 rather than at the end. Any fixture in them that relied on a phone country to reach a national holiday set now needs a stated country instead — that is the change working, not a regression, but it must be recognised as such rather than patched by re-adding the phone read.

risks.risk: TC-01-INT-17 needs 101 active members in one organization. Built through invitation round-trips — each of which needs an admin re-login, per the probe's own finding — it is minutes, not the half-second an integration case is supposed to cost.
risks.mitigation: Seed the memberships directly rather than through the invitation flow. The case asserts a row count against a cap; it does not need a real acceptance journey for any of the 101.

risks.risk: An unlocked write to Organization.countryCode contends with two shipped transactions that hold SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on that same row (members.service.ts:160 remove, :404 updateDetail) and one that updates it (signing-settings.service.ts:119). The write waits.
risks.mitigation: Waiting is correct and REQ-01-033 rules out a lock explicitly — one column, no read-modify-write, last-write-wins. Recorded in T4's concurrency so a reviewer does not read the missing lock as an omission.

risks.risk: The calendar's response assembles days, holidays, per-member holiday resolution and bands for up to 100 members over up to 92 days. A naive implementation resolves the country and re-tests every holiday per member per day.
risks.mitigation: Resolve each member's country once, test each holiday against each member once (holidays in a 92-day window are a handful), and emit holidayIds per member. appliesToAllInView is one pass over the resolved rows. No case measures this and none should; it is named here so the shape is chosen deliberately rather than discovered.

notes: Nothing in this spec was found unplannable. The three findings recorded in the verdict are notes — one incomplete premise about a fixture helper, one case whose fixture must supply an input the case does not name, and one deliberate asymmetry worth writing into the code as a comment so the next reader does not 'fix' it.
